- \(f_0\) be the horn’s emitted frequency,  
- \(v_s\) be the car’s speed relative to the air (positive when approaching).

When the car is **approaching** it is heard at a higher frequency  

\[
f_{\text{app}} = f_0\frac{v}{v-v_s}=284\ \text{Hz}.
\]

When it recedes, the lower frequency is  

\[
f_{\text{rec}} = f_0\frac{v}{v+v_s}=266\ \text{Hz}.
\]

Divide the two equations to eliminate \(f_0\):

\[
\frac{f_{\text{app}}}{f_{\text{rec}}}
   =\frac{\dfrac{v}{v-v_s}}{\dfrac{v}{v+v_s}}
   =\frac{v+v_s}{\,v-v_s\,}
   =\frac{284}{266}=\frac{142}{133}.
\]

Thus  

\[
\frac{v+v_s}{v-v_s}= \frac{142}{133}.
\]

Cross‑multiply:

\[
133(v+v_s)=142(v-v_s) \\
133v+133v_s = 142v-142v_s \\
(133+142)v_s = 142v-133v \\
275 v_s = 9v.
\]

Hence  

\[
v_s = \frac{9}{275}\,v = \frac{9}{275}\times1100\ \text{ft/s}=36\ \text{ft/s}.
\]

Convert feet per second to miles per hour (\(1\ \text{ft/s}=0.681818\ \text{mph}\)):

\[
36\ \text{ft/s}\times 0.681818\ \frac{\text{mph}}{\text{ft/s}}
   \approx 24.5\ \text{mph}.
\]

Therefore the car’s speed is about **24.5 mph**, which corresponds to option (I).

**The answer is (I)**
